dialect.guess: Micro Focus COBOL (or compatible, likely GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL used in ORCA project)
evidence: All four DIVISIONS present (IDENTIFICATION, ENVIRONMENT, DATA, PROCEDURE)
COPY statements with quoted filenames (e.g., COPY "COMMON-SPA")
OCCURS clauses, REDEFINES, VALUE clauses consistent with COBOL-85
Fixed format, max line length 74, comment lines with * in column 7

purpose.summary: This program is part of the ORCA (JMA standard receipt software) system, specifically handling ward/department management (病棟管理, byōtō kanri) for a Japanese medical institution. It manages inpatient ward configuration data including nursing ratios, room assignments, special hospitalization fees, and related master data. It appears to be a screen-driven batch/online program for system administration of hospital ward settings.
purpose.domain: healthcare/medical (Japanese hospital billing and management system)

notable_features: No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — uses proprietary MCP (Message Control Program) linkage area instead
Extensive use of COPY statements for copybooks (file layouts, subprogram parameters, screen areas)
Japanese text in comments (Shift-JIS/EUC-JP encoded, decoded as latin-1 producing mojibake)
LINKAGE SECTION with MCPAREA, ORCA-SPA, LINKAREA — typical of ORCA/JMA GUI framework
Large CONST-AREA with hardcoded medical procedure codes (診療行為コード)
REDEFINES used extensively for code tables
432 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural decomposition
Screen area copybooks (W01.INC through W09.INC) suggesting GUI screen management
verdict.notes: The file is part of the open-source ORCA (JMA standard receipt/medical billing) software from Japan Medical Association, copyright 2002. Japanese comments are encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS but decoded as latin-1, producing garbled characters. The program uses a proprietary MCP (screen/message control) framework rather than CICS, so 'online-cics' is an approximation — it is an interactive screen program within the ORCA framework. The COPY count of 0 in mechanical indicators likely reflects that COPY statements use quoted filenames which may not have been counted by the parser.
